AI Build-Out Is Far-Reaching for U.S. Economy
 
Plus, eldercare costs and the downfall and resurrection of Nvidia’s CEO
 
 
SHELBY TAUBER/REUTERS
 

The artificial-intelligence build-out has become the major force behind U.S. economic growth. But in doing so it is also pushing other areas of the economy aside.

 

The build-out is far-reaching. There is spending on data-center construction, on semiconductors and computing gear, on generators, backup batteries and cooling systems. Hotels near data centers are seeing revenue growth rise. Even snowmobile-maker Polaris said it was seeing strong demand for off-road vehicles from contractors building data centers.

 

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

When Paying for Mom and Dad’s Eldercare Rips Up Adult Kids’ Financial Future

 

The eye-popping cost of eldercare is shifting the financial burden to some adult children who weren’t expecting to foot the bill.

 
 
 

Market Talk

 

From Dow Jones Newswires

 

Home-buying demand dropped last quarter, Zillow says. Mortgage rates rose significantly from July through September, leaving fewer serious shoppers competing for each home on the market. The number of engaged home shoppers per listing, signaling real interest beyond casual browsing, fell to 3.5 nationally in 3Q. That is down 4.8% from a year earlier and the lowest level since the second half of 2023. The pullback was widespread, with engagement down from last year in 44 of the 50 largest metro areas, although major Florida markets were an exception. Mortgage rates are still keeping many buyers on the sidelines, and as inventory continues to build, there is less competition for each home for sale. (Chris Wack, chris.wack@wsj.com)

 

Direct and indirect effects of high energy costs could keep U.K. inflation well above the Bank of England 2% inflation target in 2027, Oxford Economics’ Michael Saunders says in a note. Assuming energy prices do not rise further, “the buildup of indirect effects will maintain upward pressure on core inflation throughout 2027 and into early 2028,” he says. Investors expect the BOE to increase interest rates at least three more times by July 2027 to tackle inflation, LSEG data show. The BOE raised rates 25 basis points to 4.0% at the November policy meeting. (Miriam Mukuru, miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
